newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks close down as resources fade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks close down as resources fade.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2342 -3 US 30yr cl 6.82 -0.03
S&P500(Globex) 704.90 -0.45 NZSE40 (holiday)
*Stocks ended slightly weaker after resources lost ground late in the session. Volume 330.8 million shares, value A$488.1 million, 1,005 stocks traded, 323 steady, 375 rises, 307 falls
Australian shares closed slightly weaker on Monday after a bout of selling in the resources sector in the last hour of trading.

The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed 1.1 points lower at 2,334.1, well off its intra-day high of 2,346.9. The December share price index ended up 10 points at 2,355 and at a 12.4 point premium to the underlying index.
Dealers said turnover was noticeably thin with investors cautious after the market's sharp sell-off on Friday and ahead of important U.S. economic data due out later this week.
"The market was quiet all day," a Brisbane dealer said.
"Investors that were in early wanted to be fairly square at the end of the day because Wall Street could be a volatile animal this week," he said.
The dealer said industrial issues were supported by a stronger bond market which was still confident that a local monetary easing was a near term prospect.

"Investors remain comfortable with the relatively high level of the Australian market but are less secure with a Dow above 6,000. The fear is the U.S. market has been over-inflated by the presidential election," the dealer said.
The bank sector outperformed the market on the day and ANZ stock was active after the company denied it was discussing merger plans with U.K. bank Standard Chartered.

Another strong performer was nickel hopeful Anaconda Nickel whose shares went for a run after the company announced it had placed some stock with its major shareholder, Swiss commodities group, Glencore International AG.

In other markets, Australian bonds ended slightly firmer in thin trade with rate-cut speculation underpinning gains. The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.41 percent, 0.04 percentage points down from Friday's closing level.
The Australian dollar recouped some offshore losses after early fears of a rate cut proved unfounded. At 4.55 p.m. (0555 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7924/29.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade continued to ease back after the hectic activity inspired by option expiries last week with futures business noticeably down on Friday's levels.
